name: Ausgrid – EA116 residential demand (peak seasons)
assumed: The window is Ausgrid's own and is not assumed: 15:00–21:00, **every day** (not only weekdays — a Sunday evening counts), in the June–August and November–March periods, on the highest 30-minute period of the month. Two things about the price are assumed, and both are places the grammar does not reach. (1) The unit of time. Ausgrid quotes 44.4147 c/kVA/day for EA116 in 2026-27 and multiplies it by the number of days in the month; `PeakTariff.price_period_unit` is `month` or `year`, with no `day`, so the rate is carried as a year — 0.444147 × 365 = 162.1137 AUD/kVA/year — and a month pays a twelfth of it. That averages the month length away: a 31-day month really pays about 2 % more than this says and February about 8 % less. The steering is unaffected (which half-hour matters does not depend on the rate) and only the reported fee drifts. (2) The unit of power. Ausgrid bills kVA and powerplan measures kW, and `PeakTariff` has no `unit`/`power_factor` (only `ContractedPower` does), so this preset reads the demand as kW — exact at a power factor of 1.0 and an under-estimate below it. A `price_period_unit: "day"` and a power factor on `PeakTariff` would remove both notes and are D2's call, not this WP's. The retailer, not Ausgrid, sets what the household actually pays, so the bill is an estimate of the network component either way.

versions.assumed: See the file-level note: the window is published, the price is converted from c/kVA/day and read as kW.
